# Configuration

All configuration comes from environment variables, validated at startup by
`pydantic-settings` (a bad value stops the container immediately). `.env` is
created from `.env.example` by `python -m tools.cli init`; Compose passes each
service only the variables it needs.

This file grows with the project: variables for components that are not built
yet are added in the phase that builds them.

## Secrets (generated by `init`, never committed)

| Variable | Used by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `WEBHOOK_TOKEN` | Alertmanager, agent | Bearer token for Alertmanager webhooks (also written to `.secrets/webhook_token`) |
| `APPROVER_TOKEN` | agent, CLI | Approves or rejects high-risk actions; changes agent mode |
| `CHAOS_TOKEN` | gateway, orders, CLI | `X-Chaos-Token` header for fault injection |
| `LOADGEN_TOKEN` | loadgen, CLI | `X-Loadgen-Token` header for rate changes |
| `CONSOLE_OPERATOR_KEY` | console | Operator key for mutations from the UI |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | postgres, orders | Database password |
| `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | grafana | Grafana `admin` password (anonymous users are read-only viewers) |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | agent | LLM key. Paste it into `.env` yourself; it is never generated or printed |

## General

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT_NAME` | `relialoop` | Project name |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING` or `ERROR`. Health and metrics requests are logged at `DEBUG` |

## Host ports

Every published port is bound to `127.0.0.1`. Change a value in `.env` if the
port is already in use on your machine.

| Variable | Default | Service |
|---|---|---|
| `GATEWAY_PORT` | `8000` | gateway API and chaos endpoints |
| `LOADGEN_PORT` | `8002` | loadgen control API |
| `PROMETHEUS_PORT` | `9090` | Prometheus |
| `GRAFANA_PORT` | `3000` | Grafana |

| `BAD_RELEASE_ERROR_RATE` | `0.25` | `bad` profile: share of requests failing with 500 |
| `BAD_RELEASE_LATENCY_MS` | `300` | `bad` profile: latency added to every request |
| `CRASH_RELEASE_AFTER_S` | `8` | `crash` profile: seconds after start until the process exits |
| `CHAOS_DEFAULT_DURATION_S` | `300` | Lifetime of an injected fault when none is given |
| `CHAOS_MAX_DURATION_S` | `3600` | Upper bound on a fault's lifetime |

## Loadgen

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `TARGET_URL` | `http://gateway:8000` | Where traffic is sent |
| `LOADGEN_RPS` | `20` | Baseline request rate (70% reads, 30% writes) |
| `LOADGEN_MAX_RPS` | `500` | Upper bound accepted by the control API |
| `READ_FRACTION` | `0.7` | Share of GET requests |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S` | `3.0` | Client timeout |

| `CLIENT_SHARDS` | `8` | Number of HTTP client pools the requests are spread over |

## Capacity model and measured tuning

Orders has `ORDERS_WORKERS` slots and each request holds one for
`ORDERS_WORK_MS` plus its database call, so a replica's capacity is roughly
`ORDERS_WORKERS / (ORDERS_WORK_MS / 1000)` requests per second (100 rps
nominal with the defaults). Requests beyond that queue for a slot; a request
that waits more than `ORDERS_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_S` is shed with 503, which the
gateway reports as 502. Each replica adds another set of slots, which is why
scaling out fixes a surge.

The defaults (`ORDERS_WORKERS=4`, `ORDERS_WORK_MS=40`, `LOADGEN_RPS=20`,
orders limited to 0.5 CPU and 192 MiB) were kept after measuring them on the
development machine on 2026-11-12:

| Condition | Gateway 5xx ratio | Gateway p95 | Orders worker utilization |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline 20 rps, 1 replica | 0% | about 0.10–0.12 s | 0.25 |
| Surge 150 rps, 1 replica | 44.9% | 1.95 s | 0.99 |
| Surge 150 rps, 2 replicas | 0% | 0.27 s | 0.76–0.78 |
| Surge 180 rps, 3 replicas | 0% | 0.27 s | 0.66–0.69 |

A closed-loop benchmark against a single orders replica (8 concurrent
clients, 6 s) measured 89 requests per second, so real capacity is about 89
rps rather than the nominal 100 (the database call and framework overhead add
about 7 ms per request).

Method and limits: one run per condition, each value read from Prometheus
over a 20–30 s window while the condition held, on a single machine. These
are tuning observations, not benchmark results. p95 is interpolated from
histogram buckets, so it is coarse.

Consequences for the fault scenarios:

- A **150 rps** surge clearly saturates one replica and is healthy on two, so
  the agent's "scale +1" action is enough to recover. The evaluation scenario
  (`eval/scenarios/latency_saturation.yaml`) now uses **130 rps**, which is
  still above the measured single-replica capacity of about 89 rps; the first
  evaluation run used 150 rps (see `docs/results/README.md`).
- Under saturation most errors are 502 (orders shedding load with 503), not
  504 timeouts, because requests are shed after 1.5 s, before the gateway's
  2 s timeout.

## Simulated releases

| Check (2026-11-12, one run each) | Observed |
|---|---|
| `v2-bad` at 20 rps | orders 5xx ratio 26%, gateway 5xx ratio 27%, gateway p95 0.49 s |
| `v3-crash` | 4 container restarts in about 50 s |

## Agent

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENT_MODE` | `dry_run` | `observe` (diagnose only), `dry_run` (decide and record, execute nothing) or `enforce` (act through validator and policy). Read at startup; `python -m tools.cli mode …` changes it until the next restart |
| `DIAGNOSIS_MODE` | `rules` | `rules` (deterministic decision tree) or `llm` |
| `AGENT_WORKERS` | `2` | Incidents processed in parallel |
| `AGENT_QUEUE_SIZE` | `100` | Bounded incident queue; when full, webhooks get 429 |
| `MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `262144` | Largest accepted request body (413 above) |
| `MAX_ALERTS_PER_WEBHOOK` | `100` | Most alerts accepted in one notification |
| `PROMETHEUS_URL` | `http://prometheus:9090` | Evidence and verification queries |
| `DB_PATH` | `/data/agent.db` | SQLite store (named volume `agentdata`) |
| `CMDB_PATH` | `/app/cmdb/services.yaml` | Service catalog (read-only mount) |
| `POLICY_PATH` | `/app/agent/policy.yaml` | Policy file (in the image) |
| `RUNBOOKS_DIR` | `/app/docs/runbooks` | Runbooks served at `/runbooks/<name>` |
| `VERSIONS_FILE` | `/deploy/versions.env` | Rewritten by a rollback |
| `COMPOSE_PROJECT` | `relialoop` | Only containers of this Compose project are ever touched |
| `HTTP_TIMEOUT_S` | `5` | Timeout of outbound HTTP calls |
| `DOCKER_GID` | `0` | Group that owns the Docker socket inside containers (Compose `group_add`). Docker Desktop: 0; Linux: gid of the `docker` group |

### LLM diagnosis

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `gemini` | `gemini` or `fake` (scripted; tests and CI) |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | empty | Key for the Gemini API. Only in `.env`; never logged. Without it only `DIAGNOSIS_MODE=rules` is available |
| `GEMINI_MODEL` | empty | Model to use. Empty = probe the newest flash-class model at first use. Pinning is recommended; see `docs/adr/0003-llm-provider.md` for the free-tier quota that makes this matter |
| `LLM_FAKE_FIXTURE` | unset | JSON file with scripted responses for the fake provider |
| `LLM_TIMEOUT_S` | `25` | Time limit of one LLM call |
| `LLM_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `2` | Attempts per call for retryable errors (timeout, 429, 5xx), with exponential backoff and jitter |
| `LLM_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S` | `20` | Time limit of a model-selection probe |
| `LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `4096` | Output limit; generous because reasoning tokens count against it |
| `LLM_TEMPERATURE` | `0.0` | Sampling temperature |
| `MAX_EVIDENCE_ROUNDS` | `2` | Extra rounds in which the model may request optional catalog evidence by name |
| `MAX_LLM_CALLS_PER_INCIDENT` | `3` | Hard cap on API calls for one diagnosis, retries included |
| `POSTMORTEMS_DIR` | `/postmortems` | Where postmortems are written (bind mount of `./postmortems`) |

Any LLM failure (timeout, rate limit, malformed output, exhausted call
budget) falls back to the rule-based engine and marks the incident
`degraded_mode`. `python -m tools.cli mode --diagnosis llm|rules` switches the
engine for new incidents at runtime.

### Evidence

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EVIDENCE_TIMEOUT_S` | `10` | Overall limit for collecting a bundle; on timeout the bundle is marked incomplete |
| `LOG_LINES` / `LOG_SINCE_S` | `200` / `300` | Log lines and look-back per service |
| `LOG_MAX_BYTES` / `LOG_TAIL_LINES` | `4096` / `20` | Size cap and tail length of a log summary |
| `DEPLOY_HISTORY_LIMIT` | `5` | Deploy events included per service |

### Rule-based diagnosis thresholds

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `RESTARTS_THRESHOLD` | `2` | Restarts in 2 minutes that count as a crash loop |
| `DEPLOY_RECENT_S` | `600` | A deploy this recent, with errors or latency up, is a bad deploy |
| `ERROR_RATIO_ELEVATED` | `0.05` | 1-minute 5xx ratio that counts as elevated |
| `LATENCY_P99_ELEVATED_S` | `1.0` | 1-minute p99 that counts as elevated |
| `MEMORY_PCT_THRESHOLD` | `0.7` | Share of the memory limit above which rising memory is a leak |
| `SATURATION_UTILIZATION` | `0.9` | Worker utilization that counts as saturated |
| `LOAD_SURGE_FACTOR` | `1.5` | Request rate relative to 10 minutes ago that counts as a surge |

### Validator, execution and verification

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `MIN_CONFIDENCE` | `0.6` | Diagnoses below this are rejected and escalated |
| `ROLLBACK_LOOKBACK_S` | `1800` | A rollback needs a deploy of the target this recent |
| `ACTION_TIMEOUT_S` | `90` | Time limit of one action, including waiting for health |
| `VERIFY_WAIT_S` | `20` | Wait after an action before the first check |
| `VERIFY_INTERVAL_S` | `10` | Time between checks |
| `VERIFY_TIMEOUT_S` | `120` | Give up verifying after this long |
| `VERIFY_CONSECUTIVE` | `3` | Healthy checks in a row needed to call it recovered |
| `FAST_BURN_FACTOR` / `RECOVERY_BURN_FRACTION` | `14.4` / `0.5` | Recovered when the short-window burn rate is below factor x fraction (7.2) |
| `VERIFY_BURN_WINDOW` | `30s` | Burn-rate window used for verification |
| `MAX_REPLANS` | `1` | Re-plans after a failed verification before escalating |

Risk classes, approval timeout and action limits are not environment
variables: they live in `agent/policy.yaml`, which is reviewed like code.

## Deploy gate

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GATE_MIN_BUDGET` | `0.25` | A deploy is blocked when any SLO of the service has less error budget left than this |
